jobs.description: The University of Nevada, Reno (UNR) appreciates your interest in employment at our growing institution. We want your application process to go smoothly and quickly. Final applications must be submitted prior to the close of the recruitment. If you need assistance or have questions regarding the application process, please contact our recruitment helpline at (775) 784-1495 or jobs@unr.edu . Job Description The Orvis School of Nursing at the Carnegie R1-designated University of Nevada, Reno seeks an inaugural embedded Nurse Scientist within its academic-practice partnership with Renown Health. The Nurse Scientist will work alongside clinical nurses, nursing leaders, and interprofessional teams to generate new knowledge, investigate the impact of nursing care, and advance nursing science. This is a role for a builder. The successful candidate will develop the relationships, infrastructure, and culture that make nursing inquiry integral to clinical practice and organizational decision-making, while advancing an independent program of scholarship. We welcome candidates across career stages who demonstrate a clear scholarly focus, strong methodological preparation, and the capacity to develop a funded program of research. The successful candidate will bring the vision and collaborative approach needed to build a new program, whether developing an emerging research portfolio or bringing an established body of scholarship to this opportunity. Key Responsibilities Build the nursing research enterprise Develop and implement a strategic agenda for nursing research across the partnership. Build sustainable infrastructure for nurse-initiated research, including consultation, project development, data access, and grant support. Contribute leadership to nursing research councils, committees, and strategic initiatives. Advance nursing science and outcomes research Develop and sustain a focused program of research aligned with your outcomes-focused area of expertise. Translate findings into clinical protocols, care models, policies, and delivery improvements. Partner with nurses and clinical leaders Collaborate with frontline nurses, advanced practice registered nurses, educators, nursing leaders, and quality teams to develop clinically relevant research questions. Serve as a trusted methodological partner, designing rigorous evaluations of nursing interventions, workforce programs, and quality initiatives. Develop capacity and external funding Mentor nurses, students, faculty, clinicians, and emerging investigators, and build collaborative research teams across clinical, academic, and community settings. Pursue extramural funding from federal, foundation, industry, and other sources appropriate to your career stage. Appointment and Support This is an open-rank faculty position with two pathways. Rank, pathway, and workload are determined by the candidate's qualifications, experience, scholarly trajectory, and career goals. Tenure-track. Develop or maintain an active program of research and scholarship while contributing to the teaching, mentoring, and service missions of the school. Expectations align with rank and career stage. Research-focused non-tenure-track. Contribute primarily through research, scholarship, capacity building, and service to the partnership. Teaching responsibilities, if any, are determined by mutual agreement and organizational need. Consideration for an endowed professorship may be available for an appropriately qualified candidate. The Nurse Scientist works in close partnership with the Chief Nurse Executive and nursing leaders across Renown Health, serves as a leader within the school's Center for Nursing Outcomes Research and Office of Research and Scholarly Impact, and has direct access to clinical leaders, frontline nurses, quality and safety teams, and research opportunities across diverse healthcare settings. Job Description The University of Nevada, Las Vegas invites applications for Assistant Professor in Evolutionary Biology, School of Life Sciences [ R0153361]. Starting in Fall 2027 ROLE of the POSITION The School of Life Sciences at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in Evolutionary Biology. The ideal candidate will establish an integrative research program that investigates the processes and drivers of adaptation using modern experimental, genomic, and/or computational approaches, including adaptation to extreme or rapidly changing environments. We are particularly interested in researchers exploring a mechanistic understanding of how non-genetic processes, such as epigenetic regulation, interface with genetic variation to effect phenotypic variation and adaptation. The candidate will be expected to integrate their research program with the mission of the School of Life Sciences and to collaborate with existing faculty across multiple areas of expertise, including local adaptation and speciation; host–microbiome and plant–pest coevolution; and organismal physiology in extreme environments. Additional collaborative opportunities exist in the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry. The University's location in the Mojave Desert also offers opportunities to study adaptation in a natural extreme-environment system, though research need not be tied to any particular study system or environment. The successful applicant is expected to establish a rigorous research program supported by extramural funding, generate peer-reviewed scholarship, mentor and advise graduate students, teach effectively at the undergraduate and graduate levels (focus on evolutionary biology, epigenetics, molecular ecology, or mechanisms of adaptation) and engage in service activities. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS This position requires a Ph.D. in a biological science related degree from an accredited college or university as recognized by the United States Department of Education and/or the Council on Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA). Credentials must be obtained prior to the start date. The successful applicant will demonstrate a proven record of research accomplishment. BACKGROUND SCREENNING Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a pre-employment background screening. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Post-doctoral research training will be favorably considered . COMMITMENT to DIVERSITY and CAMPUS VALUES A successful candidate will support diversity, equity, and inclusiveness and contribute to a respectful, positive work environment. They will use our Campus Values to guide their decisions and actions and demonstrate our Rebel spirit. SALARY Salary competitive with those at similarly situated institutions. BENEFITS OF WORKING AT UNLV Competitive total rewards package including: Paid time off, sick leave, and holidays Excellent health insurance including medical, dental and vision Comprehensive retirement plans and voluntary benefits programs No state income tax Tuition discounts at Nevada System of Higher Education (NSHE) schools Tuition discounts for spouses, domestic partners, and dependents PERKS & PROGRAMS Employee

Job Description The Department of Nutrition at the University of Nevada, Reno invites applications for the position of Department Chair at the Associate/Full Professor level. The purpose of this position is to build on the Department’s strengths in nutrition. We are seeking a candidate with demonstrated success as a leader in higher education, and a distinguished record of teaching and scholarship within the area(s) of Nutrition. The Department of Nutrition is one of four academic units within the College of Agriculture, Biotechnology, and Natural Resources. The college also includes the Nevada Agricultural Experiment Station and Extension. The Department offers both BS and MS degrees in Nutrition; a Nutrition minor; and two accredited dietetic programs. The Department’s cutting-edge scholarly efforts span the continuum of basic, translational, and applied research in nutrition and dietetics. The interdisciplinary nature of nutrition is reflected in the Department’s successful collaborations with the School of Medicine, School of Public Health, Extension, and other academic units. The Department faculty currently consists of state-funded tenured/tenure-track positions (7.0 FTE) and lecturers (3.0 FTE); sponsor-funded positions (2.5 FTE); and part-time instructors (1.0 FTE). Opportunities and resources will become available for the incoming Chair to build the Department’s PhD program in nutrition. Future goals include the building of a Food Science program in the Department. Major Responsibilities Provide visionary leadership to the Department that serves to effectively broaden its mission. Lead departmental efforts to achieve short-and long-term goals for instruction, research, and outreach consistent with that of a Carnegie R1 institution. Provide administrative oversight to all programs, including both accredited dietetic programs (DI and DPD). Support, foster, and encourage the Department’s culture to continue to promote diversity, equity, and inclusion. Manage human, financial, and physical resources to maximize effectiveness and efficiencies. Work collaboratively with college and university leadership; faculty and staff; and other stakeholders to advance the mission of the Department. Represent and advocate for the Department faculty, staff, students, and programs. Recruit, develop, and retain a team of faculty, staff, and students that exhibits and values excellence and innovation. Cultivate impactful relationships with community leaders, industry, and other stakeholders. Maintain a successful research program.
